question: Uraiyur, a place famous for cotton, was the political centre (capital) of the:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Cholas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Uraiyur** was an ancient Chola capital situated near present-day Tiruchirappalli in Tamil Nadu.
 
• The Cholas were one of the longest-ruling dynasties in South Indian history, with a history spanning over several centuries.
 
• Uraiyur was not only a political center but also known for its flourishing cotton trade, contributing to the economic prosperity of the Chola kingdom.
 
• The Cholas made significant contributions to art, architecture, and literature during their rule, leaving a lasting legacy in South India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chalukyas**

 
 
• The Chalukya dynasty ruled large parts of southern and central India between the 6th and the 12th centuries.
 
• They were known for their architectural achievements, including the rock-cut temples at Badami and the structural temples at Aihole and Pattadakal.
 
 
 
• **Pandyas**
 
 
• The Pandya dynasty was one of the ancient Tamil dynasties, with their capital at Madurai.
 
 
• **Cheras**
 
 
• The Chera dynasty was an ancient Dravidian Tamil dynasty that ruled over parts of present-day Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
 
• They are well-known for their trade relations with the Roman Empire and their contributions to Tamil literature.
 
 
 
• **Cholas**
 
 
• The Chola dynasty was a Tamil dynasty that ruled from the 9th to the 13th century.
